speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh
text: asked the Minister for Digital Development and Information (a) whether the Government was consulted prior to GovTech's decision to proceed with its operating-model transformation and the retrenchment of affected employees on the current timetable; and (b) if so, what the Government's assessment was of the feasibility of phasing the retrenchment over a longer period.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: asked the Minister for Digital Development and Information (a) whether the Ministry had (i) anticipated GovTech's shift towards a continuous product ownership model and (ii) directed timely upskilling or career conversion programmes to be implemented to reduce retrenchments; and (b) of the officers affected by the restructuring, whether the Ministry has information on (i) how many have secured new employment and (ii) what career transition and reskilling support has been provided.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Digital Development and Information (a) whether GovTech's move from project delivery to product ownership reflects a broader shift in public sector technology hiring; (b) how the Government's demand for project, vendor-management and product-development roles is expected to change; and (c) what implications these have for the wider technology workforce, including mid-career workers and their retraining pathways.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: asked the Minister for Digital Development and Information in light of recent GovTech retrenchments (a) whether the Ministry has assessed if Singapore has a sufficient pipeline of talent to support the growing demand for capabilities in digital product management and product ownership across the public and private sectors; and (b) what measures, if any, are being taken with industry and Institutes of Higher Learning to strengthen these capabilities among Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: If Members are satisfied with the reply, they may wish to withdraw their questions after this session.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: I would first like to acknowledge that this is a difficult transition for the affected officers and their families.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: With that in mind, let me explain what GovTech has done internally, how we intend to strengthen conviction in our public mission and how we are continuing to support our officers through this change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: The Ministry was consulted on GovTech's workforce transformation plan and we support it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: The transformation will be implemented progressively over two years to give officers time to adjust.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: GovTech will also incorporate lessons learnt from each phase.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: The workforce transformation is a necessary part of GovTech's shift from a one-off project-delivery model to a continuous product-ownership model.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: GovTech's workforce will grow because of this shift, but its composition will also need to change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: GovTech officers will need to take greater end-to-end responsibility for the digital products and platforms that the public interact with, while continuing to partner with the industry where vendors bring specialised expertise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: Teams that own the products must not only design and build them, but must also maintain and improve them continually, to provide more reliable, secure and responsive digital services for our citizens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: GovTech is therefore hiring more software engineers, product managers, designers, data specialists, cybersecurity experts and platform engineers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: However, as GovTech builds more products and operates them in-house, it will need fewer officers doing traditional project and vendor management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: GovTech anticipated this need to reshape its workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: For several years, through natural attrition and targeted recruitment, its workforce profile has shifted, but not enough to meet our needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: Therefore, GovTech has also invested heavily in pilots and apprenticeships to retrain existing staff for new roles or to redeploy them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: But there are limits to its pace and scale.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: Meanwhile, technology is changing fast and GovTech must keep up, because if we fall behind, the quality of our digital products and services for our citizens will suffer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: We will retrain and redeploy as many officers as we can, but we cannot avoid having to transition out some officers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: We recognise the disruption this causes to the affected officers and their families, and we will support them fully through this process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: In deciding whether to retain, place on apprenticeship pathways or retrench officers, GovTech first assessed the job roles it needed for its future organisational and capability needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: Then, it assessed individual officers based on their competencies, domain expertise, job fit and readiness for the roles required.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: GovTech also consulted technology leaders in our agencies, including Chief Information Officers and Practice Leads, but it took the final workforce decisions centrally.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: Among the 93 exiting officers, the largest age group is 40 to 49.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: This age group accounts for 42% of the exiting officers and also, 42% of the 305 affected officers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: This age group is therefore not over-represented among the exiting officers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: There is no significant difference in tenure between the exiting officers and those on retraining pathways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: The exiting officers have served for a median of 5.4 years, compared to a median of 6.0 years for the officers on retraining pathways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: As for seniority, two-thirds of the affected officers were individual contributors and one-third of the affected officers were Team Leaders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: GovTech decided to be upfront in informing the affected officers about the transition plans, to help them evaluate possible redeployment opportunities against other options.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: Where there was a suitable pathway, GovTech has retrained and redeployed its officers before considering external recruitment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: The apprenticeship pathways provide full salary, structured training and on-the-job learning to support officers in developing capabilities required under GovTech's future operating model.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: Where there was no suitable role within GovTech, affected officers were supported in seeking opportunities in the public and private sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: GovTech is working with the Public Service Division, the Skills and Workforce Development Agency and the National Trades Union Congress' Employment and Employability Institute to facilitate job matching and referrals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: Officers interested in these options are currently in the application or interview stages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: Affected officers also receive financial and transition support, career guidance and active job placement assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: GovTech will take the same approach in subsequent phases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: We will strive for clarity on the roles and capabilities required, assess officers fairly against those requirements, retain and retrain where suitable, and support those who are retrenched.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: The outcomes of the transformation will be assessed across three areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: First, whether officers have been supported through meaningful transition pathways, including retraining, conversion and redeployment where appropriate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: Second, whether GovTech has strengthened the capabilities required for its future operating model.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: And third, whether GovTech successfully delivers more secure, reliable and effective digital services for Government agencies and citizens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: As the plans for subsequent phases firm up, GovTech will inform the officers affected of the timelines and the implications for them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: GovTech's leadership will continue to engage officers throughout the transformation and work closely with agencies to ensure that critical projects and public digital services remain supported during the transition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: To sustain staff morale, GovTech has conducted town halls and dialogues at the cluster, team and individual levels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: We seek to ensure that our staff understand not just what they are building, but why it matters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: This fosters a shared sense of purpose and commitment to building technology for public good.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: For the wider Public Service technology workforce, mid-career professionals in project and vendor management do bring valuable and transferable experience that can serve as useful foundations for product-oriented roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: However, these officers will still need to acquire relevant skills, such as agile delivery, user-centred design, cybersecurity and knowledge of data and cloud technologies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: We recognise that technology will continue to evolve and the skills required of technology professionals will also have to evolve in tandem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: The Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) will also equip students with product management capabilities through coursework and internships.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Acting Minister Lau, just to be clear, your answer is in response to Question Nos 19 to 25 listed in today's Order Paper?

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: I note that she has mentioned that GovTech will continue to hire talents in this space.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: And so, my question is whether the Ministry is aware of how this major restructuring effort will affect GovTech's reputation, and attractiveness for future talent acquisition and retention?

My second supplementary question has to do with whether this exercise has caused staff to be more cautious and whether that might affect GovTech's innovative culture, and what are the steps being taken to preserve the culture of innovation that is prevalent within GovTech?

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: We will continue to do our best in talent attraction and retention.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: We will explain the new roles that we are hiring for which are also closely aligned to the skills that are being taught in our IHLs today.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: And related to the second question on the innovative culture, we will have to convince all of our existing GovTech's staff and also new recruits that the way we approach our work in GovTech is in service of Singapore.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: So, it is not about being careful or innovative for the sake of doing so, but it has to be done because that is the only way that we create and deliver better services for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: As we help workers move forward, I have three supplementary questions.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Because I know this is not the end.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: The second supplementary question will be: I know some anxieties from those who are on term contracts and which are extended without being offered a permanent role.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: For GovTech's officers on contract for service or term contracts, will their roles be more impacted by this change in operatonal model for GovTech?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: And my third supplementary question is: she mentioned earlier those in the 40 to 49 years age group, they comprise 42% of those who are being affected.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: What is the percentage of those affected who were above 50 years?

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Perhaps, I will share two lessons from this first phase.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: First, on how officers experienced the transition itself.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Another lesson we have learned is that it is on how this transformation can be understood or may have been understood outside of GovTech.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Some of the messaging around this restructuring may have given the impression that GovTech intends to move all work in-house and not use vendors anymore.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Vendors continue to play an important role, particularly where they bring specialised expertise that complements our in-house teams.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: What is changing is that GovTech is taking greater ownership of the products that we build and the platforms that we deliver.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: We will be clearer on this distinction in how we communicate future phases, so that our partners and the industry understand exactly what is and what is not changing.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: On the second question on contract staff, we do have contract staff across GovTech in different roles – in cybersecurity, in data management, in user design and so on.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Sorry, can the Member repeat the third question?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I think in the letter by GovTech Chair, it was said that GovTech requires people who can define the problem, shape the architecture and more importantly, that the shift began years before the current AI wave.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: So, my original Parliamentary Question still remains, in that given that we already know that this was going to be coming a few years ago, what then is the so-called skills gap or competency gap that was really missing in these retrenched workers.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: And particularly, when they are in the age of about 40 to 49, these would be quite flexible mid-career workers.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Why is it that even as the transformation was anticipated, they were not being able to be repositioned for another role within the Public Service?

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: As I explained earlier, we have tried in different ways through apprenticeships, pilots and training programmes to convert as many of our staff as possible, and also to allow natural attrition to take place.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Unfortunately, it is the pace and the scale of the changes that have been that have required us to take the current steps.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: I think for many of our affected officers, we also want to give them a chance to consider whether the conversion to these new rules is something they want to do, because their competencies and their skillsets are still in demand, both in other Public Service agencies as well as in the private sector.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: So, we want to avail to them all opportunities possible and let them consider if there are opportunities that match their skillsets as well.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I have three supplementary questions for the Acting Minister.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: First, I think it is not very clear, so I would like the Minister to clarify if the affected 93 workers that have been retrenched have already stopped working, or alternatively, are they actually being supported through their transition while remaining on payroll?

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And if it is not that they are being supported through their transition and remaining on payroll, if this will be considered for both the current phase and subsequent phases?

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is a practice that my previous employer did and I thought it was a very good one as we transition workers out of the company.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And thirdly, will Government commit to monitoring the outcomes of these affected workers over the next six months or perhaps a year and commit to publishing them?

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: I will reverse the order in how I respond.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: We chose to inform the affected officers early after we completed our internal capability assessments and then determine which roles we needed going forward.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: We wanted to also give them early and direct communication because we think it serves to offices better.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Matching an officer to a role in other Government agencies is not something GovTech can do unilaterally by just comparing a resume against a list of vacancies.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Every receiving agency and team have their own hiring processes which include interviews and assessments for fit.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: And an officer has to actively take part in that process for a match to happen at all.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: What we have done is to give them enough time after the notification to let them do both work handover and also look for alternative opportunities around.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: I also just want to give a shout-out to all of them.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Many of them are focusing very much on the handover of the work and some even tell us that they will do that first before they look around for opportunities elsewhere.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: As automation and AI continue to reshape digital jobs, how will the Ministry ensure that the Government remains an employer that proactively invests in continuous skills renewal to prevent further redundancy?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: My second supplementary question is, does the Ministry see this as a structural change from project delivery to product ownership, especially so since we are rolling out more AI capabilities, more AI agents, and the need to manage such agents and whether the industry will see this similar change and whether we do we have sufficient talent in the pipeline to address this?

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Yes, GovTech will continue to invest in the skills of our officers.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Just to give you a sense of what apprenticeships look like and how we retrain and invest in our officers, our apprenticeships that we run for officers that have to go into new roles, they run from between 12 and 18 months.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: They are conducted on a full-time basis within a product team.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Officers gain practical experience in the role that they have been mapped to.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Every apprentice is given is an assigned mentor, clear learning objectives and they have regular developmental check-ins at key milestones throughout the 12 to 18 months, and then they go through a conversion assessment at the end of their apprenticeship period.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: This is extremely resource-intensive but also demonstrates our commitment to ensure that all suitable officers who are put through these pathways do have a good outcome at the end of it.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: The second question on whether or not it is a structural change in capabilities, I think overall, we try to explain the shift we are making towards product management and away from traditional project and vendor management roles.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: We do recognise that there are still many projects that are being managed with vendors and we also value the expertise that industry and vendors bring.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: I think, overall across the industry, while we do see some shift towards more product management roles, there is clear recognition, whether in the public or private sectors, that vendors remain a key partner in our digital ecosystem.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: And therefore, going forward, we still expect to work very, very closely with them.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: As for AI and the technologies and the benefits that AI will bring, we think that they can be brought on even as we move into product management, as long as we ensure that our product managers and software engineers have a good grounding in AI than any future products they build through a product management model can have AI already infused in them.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Yip, do you want to raise a last supplementary question?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I am not forcing you if you do not have any.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I think my question builds on Mr Sharael Taha's questions.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Minister has explained the movement towards product ownership.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, with AI fundamentally changing the economics of developing digital services, for example, reducing development time, lowering costs and enabling small teams to deliver more, how are you rethinking about reshaping the future workforce and especially in terms of capturing the productivity gains and at the same time, creating meaningful careers for our GovTech officers?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
